chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Jamil, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A man prays the two rak'ahs of the obligatory Tawaf behind the Maqam (Station of Abraham) reciting 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' and 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun'.

key_terms.خَلْفَ الْمَقَامِ: Behind the Station of Abraham (Maqam Ibrahim)
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The two units of prayer performed after the obligatory circumambulation

ai.seo_question: How many rak'ahs are in the prayer after Tawaf and which Surahs are recited?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Sunnah of performing two rak'ahs of prayer behind the Maqam Ibrahim following the obligatory Tawaf, emphasizing the recitation of Surah Al-Ikhlas and Surah Al-Kafirun. This practice highlights the spiritual significance of the Maqam as a place of divine encounter, linking the physical act of circumambulation with focused devotion. The selection of these specific Surahs underscores themes of monotheism and distinctiveness in worship, reinforcing the theological core of the Hajj ritual.
